newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods edge higher ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods edge higher ahead of holiday.

text.p: U.S. spot oil product prices edged higher Tuesday tracking NYMEX futures and slightly firmer differentials on Gulf Coast gasoline as buyers emerged to pick up early January barrels, traders said.

Activity was very thin, however, with many players out of the market ahead of the Christmas holiday on Wednesday. Most other traders vanished en masse soon after the early NYMEX close at 1300 EST (1800 GMT).

No. 2 heating oil diffs on the both the USG and New York Harbor (NYH) showed little movement, traders said, although NYH low sulfur diesel firmed 0.25 cent to 0.75 cent above January futures by midday.

Warmer-than-normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world, coupled with the lack of available line space on the Colonial pipeline has limited heating oil activity.
Conventional "M4"-grade unleaded gasoline for the 1st cycle on the Colonial Pipeline at the USG was bid at 3.10 cents under the NYMEX, up slightly more than 1.0 cent in late-morning activity.
At NYH, prompt reformulated A5 unleaded gasoline was talked between about 1.25 and 1.50 cents over the screen, slightly higher than Monday's levels.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
